title: Failure-mode review of a design under time

kcs.statement: A failure-mode review walks each component on the request path and names what happens when it dies, slows down or is cut off by a partition.

Each failure maps to a standard fix: a single point of failure to redundancy and failover, a slow dependency to a timeout plus a circuit breaker, a transient error to retry with backoff and jitter, and a duplicate request to an idempotency key.

End-to-end availability is estimated by collapsing each redundant tier with the parallel formula and multiplying the tiers in series, both valid only for independent failures, so shared dependencies such as one region or one config service are added as their own series components before converting the result to nines and yearly downtime.
In an interview, reliability belongs in the bottlenecks phase: name the top two or three failure modes of your design and their fixes rather than listing every pattern.

problem_ideas: URL shortener: list SPOFs and fixes, then compute availability with 2 LBs, 4 app servers and a primary + replica DB, all in one region

Raise a 99.5% design to 99.95%: which tier do you make redundant first, and what does the math say?
